description: Deterministic cron next-fire conformance corpus. Each case is a pure function: (expr, tz, from, n) -> [instant]. Instants are emitted as UTC epoch milliseconds AND as a local-time string with offset, so both the absolute instant and the wall-clock interpretation are diffable.
tzdata_note: Results depend on the tz database release. Node 24.7.0 uses ICU 77.1 / tzdata 2025b; Go 1.26.3 embeds tzdata 2025c. Offsets for every transition in this corpus were verified identical across both releases.

cases.why: Control: a 1-hour spring-forward. 02:30 does not exist on Mar 8. ISC cron would run it at 03:30.
Two-hour spring-forward (UTC+0 -> UTC+2). 01:30 does not exist on Mar 29. cron-parser issue #419.
Thirty-minute spring-forward (01:30 -> 02:30). 02:00 does not exist on Oct 4. Sub-hour transition.
Base offset is +12:45. Transition is a normal 60 min, so this isolates the :45 offset from the width.
Hourly across a two-hour gap: which wall-clock hours fire?
Hourly across a 30-minute gap. After the shift the wall clock sits at :30, so minute-0 fires move.
One-hour fall-back. 01:30 occurs TWICE on Nov 1. Does a daily job run once or twice?
POSIX: when BOTH day-of-month and day-of-week are restricted, they OR. No DST involved.
Only day-of-month restricted: no OR, fires on the 3rd only.
Feb 29 only exists in leap years. 2028 is the next.
Step values in the last hour of the day; checks rollover.
Sub-hour steps crossing the spring-forward instant.
Sub-hour steps crossing the repeated hour. Are the 15-min slots emitted twice?
